services.title: Garage Door Installation
services.shortDescription: Full garage door replacement, from carriage-style upgrades to insulated steel, installed and adjusted right the first time.
services.longDescription: A new garage door is one of the fastest ways to change the whole look of a house, but only if it's installed correctly. We handle the full job: pulling the old door, setting new tracks and hardware, balancing springs to the new door's weight, and programming the opener, so everything works together instead of fighting each other from day one.
features: Carriage-style, flush panel & insulated steel options
Spring balance matched to the new door
signals: A door that's dented, warped, or won't seal at the bottom
Wanting a style upgrade to match a renovated exterior
A door that's louder or heavier to lift than it used to be
Panels that are cracked or delaminating
process: Free on-site estimate - we measure the opening and talk through door styles and budget
We order the door and schedule a install date that works for you
Old door removed, new tracks and hardware set, door hung and balanced
Opener installed or reprogrammed, and the whole system tested before we leave

faq.q: How long does a new garage door take to install?
faq.a: Most single-door installs take about half a day once the door itself is on site. We'll give you a firm window when we schedule.

faq.q: Can you match my existing opener to a new door?
faq.a: Usually, yes. If your opener is older or underpowered for a heavier insulated door, we'll let you know before the install, not after.

faq.q: Do you install commercial garage doors too?
faq.a: Yes, we install and service both residential and commercial doors across Middle and West Tennessee.

services.title: Garage Door Repair
services.shortDescription: Openers, springs, cables, rollers, and tracks - diagnosed and fixed, usually the same day you call.
services.longDescription: Most garage door problems come down to a handful of parts: a broken spring, a worn cable, a dead opener, or a track that's out of alignment. We diagnose the actual cause instead of guessing, so you're not paying to replace parts that were never the problem in the first place.
signals: The door won't open or close all the way
Loud banging, grinding, or scraping when it moves
The opener runs but the door doesn't move
A visibly bent track or a door hanging crooked
process: Call us and describe what's happening - we can often narrow it down before we arrive
On-site diagnosis of the spring, cables, opener, and tracks
Straight pricing before any work starts, no surprise add-ons
Repair completed and the door cycle-tested before we leave

faq.q: Is a broken spring dangerous to leave alone?
faq.a: A broken spring puts a lot of extra strain on the opener and cables, and can lead to the door slamming down. We treat it as a priority call.

faq.q: Do you carry parts on the truck?
faq.a: Yes, common springs, cables, rollers, and opener parts are stocked on the truck, so most repairs are done in one visit.

faq.q: How fast can you get to an emergency call?
faq.a: We offer 24/7 emergency service and do our best to get to you the same day, especially if the door is stuck open.

services.title: Preventative Maintenance
services.shortDescription: A yearly tune-up that catches worn hardware, loose bolts, and out-of-balance springs before they turn into a breakdown.
services.longDescription: A garage door cycles hundreds of times a year, and the parts that make it move wear out gradually. Preventative maintenance catches worn rollers, loose hardware, and out-of-balance springs while they're still a five-minute fix, not a Saturday-night emergency call.
signals: It's been over a year since the door was serviced
The door has started running rougher or louder over time
You're prepping the house to sell
Heading into fall or winter and want it ready for the cold
process: Full inspection of springs, cables, rollers, tracks & hardware
Everything tightened, lubricated, and adjusted back to spec
Opener force and safety sensors tested
A quick rundown of anything worth keeping an eye on

faq.q: How often should a garage door be serviced?
faq.a: Once a year is a good rule of thumb for most homeowners, especially heading into the temperature swings of fall and winter.

faq.q: Will maintenance make my door quieter?
faq.a: Often, yes. A lot of the noise homeowners live with is just worn rollers or loose hardware, and both get addressed during a tune-up.

reviews.author: Susie Hall Pratt
reviews.text: We just had our really old garage doors replaced by y'all and they look so good! Can't believe how quiet they are. Very professional and friendly service. Will definitely recommend to friends and family! Thank you so much again for the prompt service!

reviews.author: Jamie Wallace
reviews.text: This was one of the best customer service experiences I've had in recent years. I reached out regarding replacing my current garage doors, as well as upgrading the openers. He responded and came by to take a look within 24 hours. He left me with books to choose from and never tried to influence my decision in any way. Extremely good with communication, which seems to be rare these days! The new doors and equipment were installed and I cannot rave enough. I would highly recommend Summers Garage Door Service to ANYONE with this need!

reviews.author: Hannah Weller
reviews.text: Summers Garage Door Service did an amazing job updating our garage door and making our door more functional to fit our needs! We definitely recommend them!

reviews.text: Prompt, experienced and very professional. Would highly recommend Chance and his crew for any garage door necessities.

faqs.q: Do you offer same-day or emergency service?
faqs.a: Yes, we offer 24/7 emergency service and do our best to get to same-day calls, especially when a door is stuck open or won't close.
We serve Middle and West Tennessee, including Cheatham, Dickson, Benton, Obion, Davidson, Montgomery, Humphreys, Williamson, Henry, and Carroll Counties. Call to confirm service at your address.

faqs.q: Do you repair openers, or only install new ones?
faqs.a: Both. We repair existing openers when it makes sense, and install and program new ones when a repair isn't worth it.

faqs.q: How do I know if I need a new spring or a whole new door?
faqs.a: A broken spring is usually just a spring. But if the door itself is old, dented, or the panels are failing, we'll tell you honestly whether a repair makes sense or a replacement is the better long-term call.
